questions.q_text: Which of the following phyla shows only the cellular level of organisation?
questions.solution: In sponges the cells are loosely arranged and act more or less independently, so the organisation is cellular; cnidarians show tissue level.

questions.q_text: The water vascular system with tube feet and a madreporite is a characteristic feature of which phylum?
questions.solution: Echinoderms alone possess a water vascular system used for locomotion, capture of food and respiration; water enters through the madreporite.

questions.q_text: Which of the following is NOT a feature of phylum Porifera?
questions.opt_a: Presence of a water transport or canal system
questions.opt_b: Choanocytes lining the spongocoel and canals
questions.solution: Nematocysts are stinging capsules of cnidoblasts found only in Cnidaria; sponges lack them and instead use a canal system with choanocytes.

questions.q_text: Cnidoblasts bearing nematocysts, used for anchorage, defence and capture of prey, are characteristic of
questions.solution: Cnidoblasts occur on the tentacles and body of cnidarians such as Hydra and Adamsia, and give the phylum its name.

questions.q_text: In Ctenophora, locomotion is brought about by
questions.opt_a: Muscular pedal waves of the foot
questions.opt_c: Eight external rows of ciliated comb plates
questions.solution: Ctenophores, commonly called sea walnuts, swim using eight rows of comb plates made of fused cilia; they are also bioluminescent.

questions.q_text: Flame cells serve as the excretory structures in
questions.solution: Flatworms such as Taenia and Fasciola excrete and osmoregulate through protonephridia or flame cells.

questions.q_text: The first animal phylum to possess a complete alimentary canal with a well developed muscular pharynx and a pseudocoelom is
questions.solution: Roundworms such as Ascaris have a tube-within-a-tube gut with both mouth and anus, and a body cavity not lined by mesoderm, that is, a pseudocoelom.

questions.q_text: Metameric segmentation of the body along with a closed circulatory system and nephridia is seen in
questions.solution: Annelids such as Nereis, Pheretima and Hirudinaria show true metamerism, a closed circulation and nephridia for excretion and osmoregulation.

questions.q_text: Malpighian tubules are the excretory organs of
questions.solution: Insects and other arthropods remove nitrogenous wastes by Malpighian tubules opening into the alimentary canal.

questions.q_text: The largest phylum of the animal kingdom, including about two-thirds of all named animal species, is
questions.solution: Arthropoda is the largest phylum; its members bear a chitinous exoskeleton and jointed appendages.

questions.q_text: A file-like rasping organ called the radula, used for feeding, is present in
questions.solution: The mouth of most molluscs contains a radula with transverse rows of teeth; the visceral hump is covered by a calcareous shell secreted by the mantle.

questions.q_text: Which of the following statements about Echinodermata is NOT correct?
questions.opt_b: Adults are radially symmetrical while larvae are bilaterally symmetrical
questions.opt_c: Excretion occurs through well developed nephridia
questions.opt_d: The endoskeleton consists of calcareous ossicles
questions.solution: Echinoderms have no excretory system at all; the other three statements are true of the phylum.

questions.q_text: In Hemichordata, the excretory organ is the
questions.solution: Balanoglossus has a body divided into proboscis, collar and trunk, and excretes through the proboscis gland.

questions.q_text: Which of the following is NOT a fundamental characteristic of phylum Chordata?
questions.solution: Chordates have a dorsal, hollow, single nerve cord; a ventral, solid and double nerve cord is a non-chordate feature.

questions.q_text: In which group of chordates is the notochord present only in the larval tail?
questions.solution: In urochordates such as Ascidia, Salpa and Doliolum the notochord is restricted to the tail of the larva and is lost in the adult.

questions.q_text: In Branchiostoma, the notochord
questions.opt_b: Extends from head to tail and persists throughout life
questions.opt_c: Is present only in the embryo
questions.opt_d: Is replaced by a vertebral column
questions.solution: Branchiostoma or Amphioxus is a cephalochordate in which the notochord runs the whole length of the body and is retained in the adult.

questions.q_text: Petromyzon and Myxine are placed in which class of vertebrates?
questions.solution: Cyclostomes are jawless ectoparasites of fishes with a sucking circular mouth and 6 to 15 pairs of gill slits.

questions.q_text: Placoid scales, a ventrally placed mouth and the absence of an air bladder are characteristics of
questions.solution: Cartilaginous fishes such as Scoliodon and Pristis lack an air bladder and must swim constantly to avoid sinking.

questions.q_text: Which of the following pairs of animal and its phylum is correctly matched?
questions.solution: Adamsia, the sea anemone, is a cnidarian; Aurelia is also a cnidarian, Pleurobrachia is a ctenophore and Fasciola is a flatworm.

questions.q_text: How many of the following are bony fishes: Exocoetus, Pristis, Hippocampus, Trygon, Labeo, Carcharodon?
questions.solution: Exocoetus, Hippocampus and Labeo are Osteichthyes; Pristis, Trygon and Carcharodon are cartilaginous fishes.

questions.q_text: Which of the following animals is an amphibian?
questions.solution: Ichthyophis is a limbless amphibian; Hemidactylus is a reptile, Pteropus a mammal and Neophron a bird.

questions.q_text: Among reptiles, a four-chambered heart is found in
questions.solution: Reptiles usually have a three-chambered heart with an incompletely divided ventricle, but crocodiles possess four chambers.

questions.q_text: Which of the following is NOT a characteristic of class Aves?
questions.opt_b: Air sacs connected to the lungs
questions.opt_d: An oil gland at the base of the tail
questions.solution: Birds lack a urinary bladder, an adaptation that reduces weight for flight; the other three features are typical avian characters.

questions.q_text: How many of the following statements are correct? (i) In Urochordata the notochord is present only in the larval tail. (ii) All vertebrates are chordates but all chordates are not vertebrates. (iii) In vertebrates the notochord is replaced during embryonic development by a bony or cartilaginous vertebral column. (iv) Cyclostomes possess paired fins and jaws.
questions.solution: Statements (i), (ii) and (iii) are correct; cyclostomes are jawless and lack paired fins, so (iv) is wrong.

questions.q_text: The epithelium lining the alveoli of the lungs and the walls of blood vessels is
questions.solution: A single layer of thin flattened cells forms the squamous epithelium, which is suited for diffusion of gases and filtration.

questions.q_text: Simple cuboidal epithelium in the human body is typically found in the
questions.opt_b: Proximal convoluted tubule of the nephron
questions.solution: Cuboidal epithelium lines the ducts of glands and the tubular parts of nephrons, where it also helps in secretion and absorption.

questions.q_text: Ciliated epithelium is best suited for
questions.opt_c: Moving particles or mucus in a specific direction
questions.solution: Cilia lining the bronchioles and the fallopian tubes beat to push mucus or the ovum along the tract.

questions.q_text: Which cell junction performs the function of stopping substances from leaking across a tissue?
questions.solution: Tight junctions seal adjacent cells together; adhering junctions cement cells and gap junctions allow communication between cytoplasms.

questions.q_text: Goblet cells of the alimentary canal are an example of
questions.solution: Goblet cells are isolated glandular cells that secrete mucus through the free surface, so they are unicellular exocrine glands.

questions.q_text: Which of the following is NOT a type of connective tissue?
questions.solution: Neuroglia are supporting cells of neural tissue; areolar and adipose tissues are loose connective tissue and blood is a fluid connective tissue.

questions.q_text: Tendons and ligaments are examples of
questions.solution: In dense regular tissue the collagen fibres are arranged in parallel bundles; tendons attach skeletal muscle to bone and ligaments attach bone to bone.

questions.q_text: The cells of cartilage that lie enclosed in small cavities within the matrix are called
questions.solution: Chondrocytes occupy spaces called lacunae in the solid but pliable cartilage matrix made of chondroitin salts.

questions.q_text: Which of the following structures is supported by cartilage in adult humans?
questions.opt_b: Tip of the nose and pinna of the ear
questions.solution: Cartilage is present in the tip of the nose, the external ear joints, between adjacent vertebrae and at the ends of long bones.

questions.q_text: Intercalated discs are a distinguishing feature of
questions.solution: Cardiac muscle fibres are joined end to end by communication junctions called intercalated discs, which allow the heart to contract as a unit.

questions.q_text: Smooth muscle fibres differ from skeletal muscle fibres in being
questions.solution: Visceral or smooth muscle has no striations, is spindle shaped and is under involuntary control; skeletal muscle is striated and voluntary.

questions.q_text: Which statement about neuroglial cells is correct?
questions.opt_a: They conduct nerve impulses over long distances
questions.opt_b: They constitute more than one half of the volume of neural tissue
questions.opt_c: They are excitable and generate action potentials
questions.opt_d: They are absent in the central nervous system
questions.solution: Neuroglia protect and support neurons and make up more than half the volume of neural tissue, but they do not conduct impulses.

questions.q_text: The scientific name of the common Indian bullfrog studied as a type animal is
questions.solution: Rana tigrina is the Indian bullfrog; it is a poikilotherm that undergoes hibernation in winter and aestivation in summer.

questions.q_text: In a male frog, the copulatory pad is present on
questions.opt_b: The first digit of the forelimb
questions.opt_c: The ventral surface of the abdomen
questions.opt_d: The dorsal surface of the head
questions.solution: Males are distinguished by a pair of vocal sacs and a copulatory pad on the first digit of the forelimb, which helps in gripping the female during amplexus.

questions.q_text: When a frog is inside water, respiration takes place mainly through
questions.opt_c: The moist skin by simple diffusion
questions.opt_d: Gills retained from the tadpole stage
questions.solution: Cutaneous respiration through the moist, highly vascular skin occurs in water, while pulmonary respiration through the lungs occurs on land.

questions.q_text: The heart of a frog consists of
questions.solution: The frog heart is three chambered, with two atria and a single undivided ventricle, and is also provided with a sinus venosus and a conus arteriosus.

questions.q_text: Which of the following statements about frog blood is correct?
questions.opt_a: Red blood cells are enucleated as in humans
questions.opt_b: Red blood cells are nucleated and contain haemoglobin
questions.opt_c: Blood lacks haemoglobin and is colourless
questions.opt_d: Blood circulates in an open circulatory system
questions.solution: Frogs have a closed circulation with nucleated, haemoglobin-containing red blood cells, unlike mammalian erythrocytes which lose the nucleus.

questions.q_text: In a frog, the testes are connected to the kidneys by
questions.solution: Ten to twelve vasa efferentia arise from each testis, enter the kidney and open into the Bidder's canal, so sperms pass out through the urinogenital duct.

questions.q_text: How many pairs of cranial nerves arise from the brain of a frog?
questions.solution: The frog brain gives off ten pairs of cranial nerves, whereas mammals including humans have twelve pairs.

questions.q_text: How many of the following statements about the frog are correct? (i) It is ureotelic and excretes through mesonephric kidneys. (ii) Fertilisation is internal and development is direct. (iii) The alimentary canal, the urinary duct and the genital duct open into a common chamber called the cloaca. (iv) The liver is bilobed and secretes bile that is stored in the gall bladder.
questions.solution: Statements (i), (iii) and (iv) are correct; in frogs fertilisation is external and development is indirect through a tadpole larva, so (ii) is wrong.

questions.q_text: In earthworms, exchange of respiratory gases takes place through
questions.opt_a: The moist cuticle of the body surface
questions.solution: Earthworms have no special respiratory organ; gases diffuse across the thin, moist and vascular cuticle.

questions.q_text: Which of the following is NOT a part of the conducting zone of the human respiratory system?
questions.solution: The conducting part carries and conditions air up to the terminal bronchioles; the alveoli and their ducts form the respiratory or exchange part.

questions.q_text: The trachea of a human being divides into the right and left primary bronchi at the level of the
questions.solution: The trachea extends up to the mid thoracic cavity and bifurcates at the level of the fifth thoracic vertebra.

questions.q_text: The fluid present between the two layers of the pleura
questions.opt_a: Carries oxygen directly to the alveoli
questions.opt_b: Reduces friction on the lung surface during breathing
questions.opt_d: Produces surfactant to prevent alveolar collapse
questions.solution: Pleural fluid in the narrow space between the parietal and visceral pleurae lubricates the lung surface so it can move freely during ventilation.

questions.q_text: During normal inspiration in humans
questions.opt_a: The diaphragm and external intercostal muscles contract and the ribs and sternum move up and outward
questions.opt_b: The diaphragm relaxes and the ribs move downward
questions.opt_c: Only the internal intercostal muscles contract
questions.opt_d: The volume of the thoracic cavity decreases
questions.solution: Contraction of the diaphragm and external intercostals increases thoracic and pulmonary volume, lowering intrapulmonary pressure below atmospheric pressure by about 1 mm Hg.

questions.q_text: The normal rate of breathing in a healthy adult human at rest is about
questions.solution: A healthy human breathes 12 to 16 times a minute; the volumes exchanged are estimated with a spirometer.

questions.q_text: If the tidal volume of a person is 500 mL and the breathing rate is 12 per minute, the volume of air exchanged per minute is
questions.solution: Pulmonary ventilation equals tidal volume multiplied by breathing rate, that is 500 mL x 12 = 6000 mL per minute.

questions.q_text: For a person with tidal volume 500 mL, inspiratory reserve volume 3000 mL, expiratory reserve volume 1100 mL and residual volume 1200 mL, the vital capacity is
questions.solution: Vital capacity = ERV + TV + IRV = 1100 + 500 + 3000 = 4600 mL; residual volume is not included.

questions.q_text: Using the same values as a tidal volume of 500 mL, expiratory reserve volume of 1100 mL and residual volume of 1200 mL, the functional residual capacity of the person is
questions.solution: Functional residual capacity = ERV + RV = 1100 + 1200 = 2300 mL, the air left in the lungs after a normal expiration.

questions.q_text: If the tidal volume is 500 mL and the inspiratory reserve volume is 3000 mL, the inspiratory capacity of that person is
questions.solution: Inspiratory capacity = TV + IRV = 500 + 3000 = 3500 mL, the total volume inspired after a normal expiration.

questions.q_text: A person has a vital capacity of 4600 mL and a residual volume of 1200 mL. His total lung capacity is
questions.solution: Total lung capacity = vital capacity + residual volume = 4600 + 1200 = 5800 mL.

questions.q_text: Residual volume is the volume of air
questions.opt_a: Remaining in the lungs even after a forcible expiration
questions.opt_b: Inspired during a normal quiet inspiration
questions.opt_c: Expired during a forced expiration after a normal expiration
questions.opt_d: Present in the conducting airways only
questions.solution: Residual volume, about 1100 to 1200 mL, cannot be expelled and keeps the alveoli patent for continued gas exchange.

questions.q_text: The partial pressure of oxygen in the alveoli of a healthy human is approximately
questions.solution: Alveolar pO2 is about 104 mm Hg against 95 mm Hg in oxygenated blood and 40 mm Hg in deoxygenated blood and tissues.

questions.q_text: The respiratory rhythm centre that primarily regulates respiration is located in the
questions.solution: The respiratory rhythm centre lies in the medulla region of the brain; a pneumotaxic centre in the pons can moderate its function.

questions.q_text: What percentage of oxygen is transported by red blood cells in the blood?
questions.solution: Nearly 97 per cent of oxygen is carried by haemoglobin inside the erythrocytes and only about 3 per cent is dissolved in the plasma.

questions.q_text: The percentage of carbon dioxide transported in the blood in the form of bicarbonate is about
questions.solution: Around 70 per cent of CO2 travels as bicarbonate, 20 to 25 per cent as carbamino-haemoglobin and about 7 per cent dissolved in plasma.

questions.q_text: Carbon dioxide bound to the amino groups of haemoglobin and carried as carbamino-haemoglobin accounts for
questions.opt_a: 20 to 25 per cent of total CO2 transport
questions.opt_b: 70 per cent of total CO2 transport
questions.opt_c: 7 per cent of total CO2 transport
questions.opt_d: 97 per cent of total CO2 transport
questions.solution: Binding of CO2 with haemoglobin is favoured by high pCO2 and low pO2 at the tissues and accounts for about one fifth to one fourth of CO2 carriage.

questions.q_text: The solubility of carbon dioxide in blood as compared with that of oxygen is about
questions.solution: Because CO2 is 20 to 25 times more soluble, a much larger fraction of it can be carried dissolved in the plasma than of oxygen.

questions.q_text: The enzyme carbonic anhydrase, which speeds up the interconversion of CO2 and carbonic acid, is present in very high concentration in
questions.solution: Carbonic anhydrase occurs in high concentration in erythrocytes and in negligible amounts in plasma, so bicarbonate formation occurs mainly inside the RBC.

questions.q_text: The oxygen dissociation curve of haemoglobin shifts to the right under which set of conditions?
questions.opt_a: High pO2, low pCO2 and low temperature
questions.opt_b: High pH, low H+ concentration and low temperature
questions.opt_c: Low pCO2, high pH and high pO2
questions.opt_d: Low pH, high pCO2 and high temperature
questions.solution: A rightward shift means reduced affinity and greater unloading of oxygen; this occurs in active tissues where pCO2, H+ and temperature are high.

questions.q_text: In the alveoli, the conditions that favour the formation of oxyhaemoglobin are
questions.opt_a: Low pO2, high pCO2, high H+ concentration and higher temperature
questions.opt_b: High pO2, low pCO2, low H+ concentration and lower temperature
questions.opt_c: High pO2, high pCO2 and high H+ concentration
questions.opt_d: Low pO2, low pCO2 and low temperature
questions.solution: At the alveolar surface a high pO2 with low pCO2, low H+ and lower temperature drives oxygen loading onto haemoglobin; the reverse set operates at the tissues.

questions.q_text: Plasma constitutes what percentage of the total volume of human blood?
questions.solution: Blood is a fluid connective tissue in which plasma forms nearly 55 per cent and the formed elements about 45 per cent of the total volume.

questions.q_text: The plasma protein chiefly responsible for maintaining the osmotic balance of blood is
questions.solution: Of the 6 to 8 per cent plasma proteins, albumins maintain osmotic balance, globulins take part in defence and fibrinogens in coagulation.

questions.q_text: Serum differs from plasma in that serum
questions.opt_a: Contains no plasma proteins at all
questions.opt_d: Is plasma from which the clotting factors have been removed
questions.solution: When blood is allowed to clot, the clotting proteins such as fibrinogen are used up and the straw coloured fluid left behind is serum.

questions.q_text: The normal red blood cell count in a healthy adult human is about
questions.opt_a: 5.0 to 5.5 million per cubic millimetre of blood
questions.opt_b: 6000 to 8000 per cubic millimetre of blood
questions.opt_c: 1.5 to 3.5 lakh per cubic millimetre of blood
questions.opt_d: 12 to 16 million per cubic millimetre of blood
questions.solution: Erythrocytes number about 5 to 5.5 million per cubic mm; 6000 to 8000 per cubic mm is the leucocyte count.

questions.q_text: Red blood cells have an average life span of about 120 days after which they are destroyed in the
questions.solution: The spleen is called the graveyard of red blood cells because worn out erythrocytes are destroyed there.

questions.q_text: Which type of leucocyte is the most abundant in human blood?
questions.solution: Neutrophils form 60 to 65 per cent of the total white blood cells and are actively phagocytic in their action.

questions.q_text: The leucocytes that secrete histamine, serotonin and heparin and are involved in inflammatory responses are
questions.solution: Basophils are the least abundant granulocytes, about 0.5 to 1 per cent, and release these mediators of inflammation.

questions.q_text: Which of the following is NOT a granulocyte?
questions.solution: Lymphocytes and monocytes are agranulocytes; neutrophils, eosinophils and basophils have granular cytoplasm.

questions.q_text: Blood platelets are produced from
questions.solution: Platelets are cell fragments budded off from megakaryocytes and number 1.5 to 3.5 lakh per cubic mm of blood.

questions.q_text: A person with blood group AB can receive blood from all ABO groups because his or her plasma
questions.opt_a: Contains both anti-A and anti-B antibodies
questions.opt_d: Contains neither anti-A nor anti-B antibody
questions.solution: Group AB red cells carry both A and B antigens, so no antibodies against them are present in the plasma, making AB the universal recipient.

questions.q_text: Which ABO blood group is known as the universal donor?
questions.solution: Group O red cells carry neither A nor B antigen, so they are not agglutinated by the recipient plasma antibodies.

questions.q_text: Erythroblastosis foetalis is likely to develop when
questions.opt_a: An Rh positive mother carries an Rh negative foetus for the first time
questions.opt_b: Both mother and foetus are Rh negative
questions.opt_c: An Rh negative mother carries her first Rh positive foetus
questions.opt_d: An Rh negative mother carries an Rh positive foetus in a subsequent pregnancy
questions.solution: The first delivery sensitises the Rh negative mother, and in later pregnancies her anti-Rh antibodies cross the placenta and destroy the foetal Rh positive erythrocytes.

questions.q_text: In the process of blood coagulation, the conversion of fibrinogen into fibrin is catalysed by
questions.solution: Thromboplastin along with calcium ions converts inactive prothrombin into thrombin, and thrombin then converts soluble fibrinogen into a mesh of insoluble fibrin threads.

questions.q_text: Which of the following statements about lymph is correct?
questions.opt_a: It is a colourless fluid containing lymphocytes and is devoid of red blood cells and most large proteins
questions.opt_b: It is red in colour because it contains haemoglobin
questions.opt_c: It contains more red blood cells than blood
questions.opt_d: It circulates within the arteries and veins of the body
questions.solution: Lymph is the interstitial fluid that enters lymphatic capillaries; fats absorbed by the lacteals of intestinal villi are also carried by it.

questions.q_text: During the early part of ventricular systole, when ventricular pressure rises above atrial pressure but is still below aortic pressure,
questions.opt_a: The semilunar valves open and blood enters the aorta
questions.opt_b: The tricuspid and bicuspid valves open and blood enters the ventricles
questions.opt_c: Blood flows backward into the atria
questions.opt_d: The tricuspid and bicuspid valves close, producing the first heart sound
questions.solution: Closure of the atrioventricular valves at the start of ventricular contraction produces the first heart sound, lub; the semilunar valves open only after ventricular pressure exceeds aortic pressure.

questions.q_text: The sino-atrial node, which acts as the pacemaker of the human heart, is located in the
questions.opt_a: Upper left corner of the right atrium
questions.opt_b: Lower left corner of the right atrium
questions.opt_c: Upper right corner of the left atrium
questions.solution: The SAN lies in the right upper corner of the right atrium and generates about 70 to 75 action potentials per minute.

questions.q_text: If the stroke volume of a person is 70 mL and the heart beats 72 times per minute, the cardiac output is
questions.solution: Cardiac output = stroke volume x heart rate = 70 mL x 72 = 5040 mL, that is about 5 litres per minute in a healthy adult.

questions.q_text: In a cardiac cycle of 0.8 second duration, the joint diastole during which all four chambers are relaxed lasts for
questions.solution: The cycle is made up of joint diastole of 0.4 second, atrial systole of 0.1 second and ventricular systole of 0.3 second.

questions.q_text: In a standard electrocardiogram, the T wave represents
questions.opt_d: Return of the ventricles from the excited to the normal state
questions.solution: The T wave marks ventricular repolarisation and its end marks the end of systole; the QRS complex marks ventricular depolarisation.

questions.q_text: How many of the following statements are correct? (i) The first heart sound lub is associated with closure of the tricuspid and bicuspid valves. (ii) The second heart sound dup is associated with closure of the semilunar valves. (iii) The QRS complex represents depolarisation of the ventricles and initiates ventricular contraction. (iv) The P wave represents repolarisation of the atria.
questions.solution: Statements (i), (ii) and (iii) are correct; the P wave represents atrial depolarisation and not repolarisation, so (iv) is wrong.

questions.q_text: The dental formula of an adult human being is
questions.solution: An adult human has 2 incisors, 1 canine, 2 premolars and 3 molars in each half of each jaw, written as 2123/2123.

questions.q_text: The dental formula of the temporary (milk) dentition of a child is
questions.solution: Milk teeth lack premolars and have only two molars per half jaw, giving 2102/2102 (20 teeth in all).

questions.q_text: Salivary amylase acting in the buccal cavity hydrolyses starch mainly into
questions.solution: About 30 per cent of ingested starch is hydrolysed by salivary amylase into the disaccharide maltose at pH 6.8.

questions.q_text: Hydrochloric acid and intrinsic factor of the gastric juice are secreted by
questions.solution: Oxyntic or parietal cells of the gastric glands secrete HCl and the intrinsic factor needed for vitamin B12 absorption.

questions.q_text: The proenzyme pepsinogen of gastric juice is converted into active pepsin by
questions.solution: HCl provides the acidic pH (about 1.8) that converts pepsinogen into the active proteolytic enzyme pepsin.

questions.q_text: Inactive trypsinogen of the pancreatic juice is activated by
questions.solution: Enterokinase secreted by the intestinal mucosa converts trypsinogen into trypsin, which then activates the other pancreatic proenzymes.

questions.q_text: Which of the following statements about bile is NOT correct?
questions.opt_a: It contains the enzyme lipase that digests fats
questions.opt_b: It contains the bile pigments bilirubin and biliverdin
questions.opt_c: It emulsifies fats and breaks them into small micelles
questions.opt_d: It makes the medium alkaline and activates lipases
questions.solution: Bile contains no digestive enzymes; it has bile pigments, bile salts, cholesterol and phospholipids and only aids fat digestion.

questions.q_text: Which enzyme and substrate pair is correctly matched?
questions.solution: Lipases hydrolyse triglycerides (fats) into diglycerides, monoglycerides, fatty acids and glycerol.

questions.q_text: Which of the following enzymes is NOT a component of succus entericus (intestinal juice)?
questions.solution: Carboxypeptidase reaches the intestine as procarboxypeptidase in pancreatic juice; the others are intestinal enzymes.

questions.q_text: Glucose and amino acids are absorbed from the intestinal lumen mainly by
questions.solution: Glucose and amino acids are absorbed against a concentration gradient by active transport, which requires energy.

questions.q_text: Chylomicrons formed in the intestinal mucosal cells are released into the
questions.solution: Fat-protein droplets called chylomicrons pass into the lymph vessels (lacteals) of the villi and then into the blood stream.

questions.q_text: Water, simple sugars and alcohol are absorbed chiefly from the
questions.solution: The stomach absorbs limited amounts of water, simple sugars and alcohol, while most nutrient absorption occurs in the small intestine.

questions.q_text: The intrinsic factor secreted along with HCl is essential for the absorption of
questions.solution: The intrinsic factor of gastric juice is required for the absorption of vitamin B12 from the intestine.

questions.q_text: Cholecystokinin (CCK) released from the duodenum acts mainly on the
questions.solution: CCK stimulates the gall bladder to release bile and the pancreas to secrete pancreatic enzymes.

questions.q_text: How many of the following statements are correct? (i) Pancreatic juice contains procarboxypeptidase. (ii) Bile contains cholesterol and phospholipids. (iii) Pepsin works best at alkaline pH. (iv) Rennin is a proteolytic enzyme found in the gastric juice of infants.
questions.solution: Statements (i), (ii) and (iv) are correct; pepsin is active in the strongly acidic medium of the stomach, so (iii) is wrong.

questions.q_text: The approximate calorific values of fats and proteins respectively are
questions.solution: Fats yield about 9.0 kcal per gram whereas proteins and carbohydrates yield about 4.0 kcal per gram each.

questions.q_text: Select the correct statement regarding the histology of the human alimentary canal.
questions.opt_a: Brunner's glands are present in the submucosa of the duodenum
questions.opt_b: Crypts of Lieberkuhn lie in the serosa
questions.opt_c: The mucosa is the outermost layer of the gut wall
questions.opt_d: Goblet cells of the mucosa secrete digestive enzymes
questions.solution: Duodenal Brunner's glands occur in the submucosal layer; crypts of Lieberkuhn are mucosal, serosa is outermost and goblet cells secrete mucus.

questions.q_text: Which one of the following groups of animals is ureotelic?
questions.solution: Mammals, many terrestrial amphibians and marine fishes convert ammonia into the less toxic urea and are therefore ureotelic.

questions.q_text: Which nitrogenous excretory product requires the largest amount of water for its elimination?
questions.solution: Ammonia is the most toxic waste and is highly soluble, so its removal needs a large volume of water.

questions.q_text: The number of nephrons present in each human kidney is nearly
questions.solution: Each kidney contains nearly one million nephrons, the structural and functional units of the kidney.

questions.q_text: The glomerular filtration rate (GFR) in a healthy individual is approximately
questions.solution: The two kidneys together filter about 125 ml of filtrate per minute, which amounts to nearly 180 litres per day.

questions.q_text: Of the nearly 180 litres of filtrate formed daily, the volume of urine actually released per day is about
questions.solution: About 99 per cent of the filtrate is reabsorbed by the renal tubules, so only 1 to 1.5 litres of urine is excreted daily.

questions.q_text: Juxtaglomerular cells secrete renin in response to
questions.opt_a: A rise in glomerular blood pressure
questions.opt_c: A fall in glomerular blood flow or glomerular blood pressure
questions.opt_d: An increase in atrial natriuretic factor
questions.solution: A fall in glomerular blood flow, blood pressure or GFR activates the JG cells to release renin, starting the renin-angiotensin mechanism.

questions.q_text: Antidiuretic hormone facilitates water reabsorption mainly from the
questions.opt_a: Distal parts of the tubule, that is the DCT and collecting duct
questions.solution: ADH acts on the distal tubule and collecting duct, causing facultative reabsorption of water and preventing diuresis.

questions.q_text: Which segment of the nephron reabsorbs nearly 70 to 80 per cent of the electrolytes and water?
questions.solution: The PCT, lined by brush bordered cuboidal epithelium, reabsorbs about 70-80 per cent of electrolytes and water.

questions.q_text: The ascending limb of Henle's loop is
questions.opt_a: Permeable to water but impermeable to electrolytes
questions.opt_b: Impermeable to water but allows transport of electrolytes
questions.opt_c: Permeable to both water and electrolytes
questions.opt_d: Impermeable to both water and electrolytes
questions.solution: The ascending limb is impermeable to water but actively transports electrolytes out, so the filtrate becomes dilute as it ascends.

questions.q_text: The counter current mechanism that concentrates urine in the human kidney is maintained by
questions.opt_c: Henle's loop and the vasa recta
questions.opt_d: The ureter and the urinary bladder
questions.solution: The counter current flow in the two limbs of Henle's loop and in the vasa recta maintains the medullary concentration gradient.

questions.q_text: The osmolarity of the interstitial fluid of the kidney increases from the cortex to the inner medulla approximately from
questions.solution: NaCl and urea maintain a gradient rising from about 300 mOsmol/L in the cortex to about 1200 mOsmol/L in the inner medulla.

questions.q_text: Which of the following is NOT one of the three layers of the glomerular filtration barrier?
questions.opt_a: Endothelium of the glomerular blood vessels
questions.solution: Filtration occurs across the glomerular endothelium, the basement membrane and the podocyte layer of Bowman's capsule.

questions.q_text: The specialised epithelial cells forming the inner layer of Bowman's capsule are called
questions.solution: Podocytes are arranged so as to leave minute filtration slits through which the blood is ultrafiltered.

questions.q_text: Which of the following accessory excretory structures is NOT correctly matched with its product?
questions.opt_a: Lungs - carbon dioxide and water vapour
questions.opt_b: Liver - bilirubin, cholesterol and degraded steroid hormones
questions.opt_c: Sweat glands - NaCl, small amounts of urea and lactic acid
questions.opt_d: Sebaceous glands - excess water and mineral salts
questions.solution: Sebaceous glands eliminate sterols, hydrocarbons and waxes through sebum; they do not remove water and salts.

questions.q_text: How many of the following statements are correct? (i) Human urine is generally slightly acidic with a pH of about 6.0. (ii) An adult human excretes about 25 to 30 g of urea per day. (iii) The urinary bladder is emptied by the micturition reflex. (iv) Presence of glucose in urine is called ketonuria.
questions.solution: Statements (i), (ii) and (iii) are correct; presence of glucose in urine is glycosuria, while ketonuria refers to ketone bodies.

questions.q_text: A small amount of urea entering the thin segment of the ascending limb of Henle's loop is transported back to the interstitium by the
questions.solution: The collecting tubule returns urea to the medullary interstitium, helping to maintain the concentration gradient.

questions.q_text: Protonephridia or flame cells are the excretory structures of
questions.solution: Flame cells (protonephridia) occur in Planaria, rotifers, some annelids and the cephalochordate Amphioxus.

questions.q_text: The movement shown by macrophages and leucocytes in the human body is
questions.solution: Macrophages and leucocytes migrate by amoeboid movement brought about by pseudopodia formed by streaming of protoplasm.

questions.q_text: Ciliary movement in the human body occurs in the
questions.opt_a: Trachea and the female reproductive tract
questions.solution: Ciliated epithelium lining the trachea removes dust particles and that of the oviduct moves the ovum forward.

questions.q_text: The portion of a myofibril lying between two successive Z lines is called the
questions.solution: A sarcomere, the functional unit of contraction, extends from one Z line to the next.

questions.q_text: During contraction of a skeletal muscle fibre,
questions.opt_a: The A band shortens while the I band retains its length
questions.opt_b: The I band shortens while the A band retains its length
questions.opt_c: Both the A and I bands shorten
questions.opt_d: The length of the sarcomere remains unchanged
questions.solution: Thin filaments slide inward over the thick filaments, so the I band and H zone are reduced while the A band length stays constant.

questions.q_text: The H zone of a sarcomere represents the region
questions.opt_a: Of the A band containing only thick (myosin) filaments
questions.opt_c: Where thick and thin filaments overlap
questions.solution: The central part of the A band not reached by the thin filaments is the lighter H zone with only myosin filaments.

questions.q_text: According to the sliding filament theory, contraction of a muscle fibre takes place by
questions.opt_c: Sliding of the thin filaments over the thick filaments
questions.solution: Actin (thin) filaments slide over the myosin (thick) filaments towards the centre of the A band, shortening the sarcomere.

questions.q_text: The thin filament of a muscle fibre consists of F-actin along with
questions.solution: Two filaments of F-actin are held by two filaments of tropomyosin, with troponin distributed at regular intervals over them.

questions.q_text: During muscle contraction, Ca2+ released from the sarcoplasmic reticulum binds to
questions.opt_b: A subunit of troponin on the actin filament
questions.opt_c: The tail of the myosin molecule
questions.solution: Ca2+ binding to troponin unmasks the actin sites for myosin, allowing cross bridge formation.

questions.q_text: The globular head of heavy meromyosin bears
questions.opt_a: An ATP binding site and an active site for actin
questions.solution: The myosin head has ATPase activity and binds actin, so it forms the cross bridge that pulls the thin filament.

questions.q_text: Red muscle fibres differ from white muscle fibres in having
questions.opt_b: More sarcoplasmic reticulum and less myoglobin
questions.opt_c: Plenty of myoglobin and numerous mitochondria
questions.solution: Red fibres are rich in myoglobin and mitochondria, depend on aerobic respiration and are therefore fatigue resistant.

questions.q_text: The number of bones in the human axial and appendicular skeleton respectively is
questions.solution: The axial skeleton has 80 bones and the appendicular skeleton 126, making a total of 206 bones.

questions.q_text: The human skull is made up of
questions.opt_a: 22 bones, of which 8 are cranial and 14 are facial
questions.opt_b: 22 bones, of which 14 are cranial and 8 are facial
questions.opt_c: 24 bones, of which 8 are cranial and 16 are facial
questions.opt_d: 26 bones, of which 12 are cranial and 14 are facial
questions.solution: The cranium is formed of 8 bones and the facial region of 14 bones, totalling 22 skull bones.

questions.q_text: The human vertebral column
questions.opt_b: Has 26 vertebrae of which 7 are cervical
questions.solution: In the adult the column consists of 26 bones: 7 cervical, 12 thoracic, 5 lumbar, 1 fused sacrum and 1 coccyx.

questions.q_text: The 11th and 12th pairs of ribs are called floating ribs because they
questions.opt_a: Are attached directly to the sternum
questions.opt_b: Join the 7th rib through hyaline cartilage
questions.opt_c: Are not connected ventrally to the sternum
questions.opt_d: Have no attachment to the vertebrae
questions.solution: Floating ribs articulate with the thoracic vertebrae dorsally but have no ventral connection with the sternum.

questions.q_text: Which joint is correctly matched with its example?
questions.opt_a: Pivot joint - between the humerus and the pectoral girdle
questions.opt_c: Gliding joint - between the atlas and the axis
questions.opt_d: Ball and socket joint - between the humerus and the pectoral girdle
questions.solution: The head of the humerus fits into the glenoid cavity of the pectoral girdle forming a ball and socket joint.

questions.q_text: Myasthenia gravis is best described as
questions.opt_a: Accumulation of uric acid crystals in the joints
questions.opt_b: An autoimmune disorder affecting the neuromuscular junction and causing fatigue and weakening of skeletal muscles
questions.opt_c: Loss of bone mass due to decreased oestrogen levels
questions.opt_d: Rapid muscle spasms caused by low Ca2+ in body fluids
questions.solution: In myasthenia gravis autoantibodies impair transmission at the neuromuscular junction, producing weakness and paralysis of skeletal muscle.

questions.q_text: How many of the following statements are correct? (i) All ribs are bicephalic. (ii) The glenoid cavity of the scapula articulates with the head of the humerus. (iii) The acetabulum is formed by the fusion of the ilium, ischium and pubis. (iv) The sternum belongs to the appendicular skeleton.
questions.solution: Statements (i), (ii) and (iii) are correct; the sternum is part of the axial skeleton, so (iv) is wrong.

questions.q_text: The human neural system is divided into
questions.solution: The CNS (brain and spinal cord) processes information while the PNS consists of all the nerves associated with it.

questions.q_text: The number of pairs of cranial nerves and spinal nerves in humans respectively is
questions.solution: Twelve pairs of cranial nerves arise from the brain and 31 pairs of spinal nerves from the spinal cord.

questions.q_text: The resting membrane potential of a neuron is about
questions.solution: In a resting axon the inside is negative with respect to the outside, giving a potential difference of nearly -70 mV.

questions.q_text: The sodium-potassium pump of the neuronal membrane transports
questions.opt_d: Equal numbers of Na+ and K+ in opposite directions
questions.solution: For every ATP hydrolysed the pump moves 3 Na+ out of and 2 K+ into the cell, maintaining the ionic gradients.

questions.q_text: At the site of a nerve impulse the membrane potential reaches about +30 mV mainly because of
questions.opt_b: Rapid influx of Na+ through opened sodium channels
questions.solution: Stimulation opens voltage gated sodium channels and the resulting Na+ influx depolarises and reverses the membrane polarity.

questions.q_text: In a resting neuron the axoplasm contains
questions.opt_a: A high concentration of Na+ and a low concentration of K+
questions.opt_b: Equal concentrations of Na+ and K+
questions.opt_c: A high concentration of K+ and a low concentration of Na+
questions.solution: The axoplasm is rich in K+ and negatively charged proteins and poor in Na+, while the fluid outside shows the reverse pattern.

questions.q_text: Transmission of an impulse across an electrical synapse is
questions.opt_a: Faster than across a chemical synapse
questions.opt_b: Slower than across a chemical synapse
questions.opt_d: Always in both directions only after a delay
questions.solution: At an electrical synapse the current flows directly between the membranes, so transmission is always faster than at a chemical synapse.

questions.q_text: In a chemical synapse the neurotransmitter released from the synaptic vesicles binds to
questions.opt_a: Voltage gated Na+ channels of the pre-synaptic membrane
questions.opt_b: The myelin sheath of the axon
questions.opt_c: Nissl's granules of the cell body
questions.opt_d: Specific receptors present on the post-synaptic membrane
questions.solution: Binding of the neurotransmitter to post-synaptic receptors opens ion channels and generates a new potential in the next neuron.

questions.q_text: The myelin sheath around the axons of peripheral nerve fibres is formed by
questions.solution: In myelinated nerve fibres the axon is enveloped by Schwann cells that form the myelin sheath.

questions.q_text: The gaps left between two adjacent myelin sheaths along an axon are called
questions.solution: Nodes of Ranvier are unmyelinated gaps at which the impulse is regenerated, making conduction in myelinated fibres faster.

questions.q_text: The forebrain of humans consists of the
questions.solution: The forebrain comprises the cerebrum, thalamus and hypothalamus; pons, cerebellum and medulla form the hindbrain.

questions.q_text: Respiration and cardiovascular reflexes are controlled by the
questions.solution: The medulla contains centres that control respiration, cardiovascular reflexes and gastric secretions.

questions.q_text: Centres for the regulation of body temperature, hunger and thirst lie in the
questions.solution: The hypothalamus contains these regulatory centres and also several groups of neurosecretory cells producing hormones.

questions.q_text: The three cranial meninges arranged from outside to inside are
questions.opt_a: Pia mater, arachnoid and dura mater
questions.opt_b: Arachnoid, dura mater and pia mater
questions.opt_c: Dura mater, arachnoid and pia mater
questions.opt_d: Dura mater, pia mater and arachnoid
questions.solution: The tough outer dura mater is followed by the thin arachnoid and the innermost vascular pia mater in contact with brain tissue.

questions.q_text: The limbic system, involved in the regulation of sexual behaviour, expression of emotions and motivation, includes the
questions.solution: The inner parts of the cerebral hemispheres together with the amygdala and hippocampus form the limbic lobe or limbic system.

questions.q_text: How many of the following statements are correct? (i) The cerebral cortex appears grey because of the presence of neuron cell bodies. (ii) The two cerebral hemispheres are connected by the corpus callosum. (iii) The midbrain contains the cerebral aqueduct. (iv) Cranial nerves arise from the spinal cord.
questions.solution: Statements (i), (ii) and (iii) are correct; cranial nerves arise from the brain and not from the spinal cord.

questions.q_text: Neurons of the human cerebral cortex are mostly
questions.opt_b: Multipolar, with one axon and two or more dendrites
questions.opt_c: Bipolar, with one axon and one dendrite
questions.solution: Multipolar neurons bearing one axon and many dendrites are characteristic of the cerebral cortex; bipolar neurons occur in the retina.

questions.q_text: Which of the following is NOT an endocrine gland?
questions.solution: Salivary glands are exocrine glands that pour saliva through ducts; the others are ductless endocrine glands.

questions.q_text: Growth hormone, prolactin and thyroid stimulating hormone are secreted by the
questions.solution: The pars distalis of the anterior pituitary produces GH, PRL, TSH, ACTH, LH and FSH.

questions.q_text: Oxytocin and vasopressin are synthesised by the hypothalamus but are released from the
questions.solution: These two hormones are transported down the axons and stored in the posterior pituitary, from where they are released.

questions.q_text: Excess secretion of growth hormone in an adult results in
questions.solution: In adults excess GH causes severe disfigurement of the face and enlargement of the hands and feet, a condition called acromegaly.

questions.q_text: Dietary deficiency of iodine leads to
questions.opt_d: Hypothyroidism with enlargement of the thyroid gland
questions.solution: Iodine is essential for the synthesis of thyroxine, and its deficiency causes hypothyroidism and simple goitre.

questions.q_text: Hypothyroidism during pregnancy causes in the newborn
questions.opt_b: Stunted growth, mental retardation and deaf-mutism
questions.solution: Maternal hypothyroidism results in cretinism, marked by stunted growth, mental retardation, low IQ, deaf-mutism and abnormal skin.

questions.q_text: Thyrocalcitonin secreted by the thyroid gland
questions.solution: TCT is a hypocalcemic hormone that lowers blood Ca2+ levels and thus opposes the action of parathyroid hormone.

questions.q_text: Parathyroid hormone is called a hypercalcemic hormone because it
questions.opt_a: Stimulates bone resorption and reabsorption of Ca2+ by the renal tubules
questions.opt_b: Prevents absorption of Ca2+ from digested food
questions.opt_c: Deposits calcium salts in the bone matrix
questions.solution: PTH raises blood Ca2+ by dissolving bone matrix and by increasing Ca2+ reabsorption in the kidney and absorption from food.

questions.q_text: Thymosins secreted by the thymus gland
questions.opt_d: Promote differentiation of T-lymphocytes and provide cell mediated immunity
questions.solution: Thymosins play a major role in the differentiation of T-lymphocytes and also promote antibody production.

questions.q_text: Which of the following hormones is secreted by the adrenal medulla?
questions.solution: The adrenal medulla secretes the catecholamines adrenaline and noradrenaline, which mediate the fight or flight response.

questions.q_text: Aldosterone secreted by the adrenal cortex acts mainly on the
questions.opt_a: Renal tubules, stimulating reabsorption of Na+ and water
questions.solution: Aldosterone is a mineralocorticoid that promotes reabsorption of Na+ and water and excretion of K+ and phosphate by the kidney.

questions.q_text: Insulin and glucagon are secreted respectively by the
questions.opt_a: Alpha cells and beta cells of the islets of Langerhans
questions.opt_b: Beta cells and alpha cells of the islets of Langerhans
questions.opt_c: Acinar cells and beta cells of the pancreas
questions.opt_d: Delta cells and alpha cells of the islets of Langerhans
questions.solution: Beta cells of the islets of Langerhans secrete insulin while alpha cells secrete glucagon.

questions.q_text: Prolonged hyperglycaemia resulting from insulin deficiency leads to
questions.opt_d: Diabetes mellitus with glycosuria and formation of ketone bodies
questions.solution: Lack of insulin raises blood glucose so that glucose appears in the urine and harmful ketone bodies are produced.

questions.q_text: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
questions.solution: Interstitial or Leydig cells of the testis secrete androgens such as testosterone under the influence of LH.

questions.q_text: Steroid hormones and iodothyronines differ from protein hormones in that they
questions.opt_a: Bind to receptors present on the cell membrane
questions.opt_b: Use cyclic AMP as a second messenger
questions.opt_c: Enter the target cell and bind intracellular receptors to regulate gene expression
questions.solution: Lipid soluble hormones interact with intracellular receptors and regulate gene expression, whereas peptide hormones act through membrane receptors and second messengers.

questions.q_text: How many of the following are tropic hormones secreted by the anterior pituitary? TSH, ACTH, LH, FSH, MSH, Oxytocin
questions.solution: TSH, ACTH, LH and FSH stimulate other endocrine glands and are therefore tropic hormones; MSH and oxytocin are not.

questions.q_text: Which of the following hormone, source and function combinations is NOT correctly matched?
questions.opt_a: Atrial natriuretic factor - heart - decreases blood pressure
questions.opt_b: Erythropoietin - liver - stimulates formation of red blood cells
questions.opt_c: Melatonin - pineal gland - regulates the diurnal rhythm
questions.opt_d: Gastrin - stomach - stimulates secretion of HCl and pepsinogen
questions.solution: Erythropoietin is secreted by the juxtaglomerular cells of the kidney, not by the liver.

questions.q_text: The scrotum keeps the testes at a temperature lower than the normal internal body temperature. This difference is about
questions.solution: The scrotum acts as a thermoregulatory sac maintaining a temperature 2 to 2.5 degree C below body temperature, which is necessary for normal spermatogenesis.

questions.q_text: Androgens in the human testis are secreted by
questions.solution: Interstitial or Leydig cells lie outside the seminiferous tubules and synthesise and secrete testicular androgens under the influence of LH.

questions.q_text: Which pituitary hormone acts on the Sertoli cells and stimulates secretion of factors that help in spermiogenesis?
questions.solution: FSH acts on Sertoli cells, which then secrete factors helping the process of spermiogenesis; LH acts on Leydig cells instead.

questions.q_text: The number of chromosomes present in a human secondary spermatocyte is
questions.solution: The first meiotic division of the diploid primary spermatocyte (46) yields haploid secondary spermatocytes with 23 chromosomes each.

questions.q_text: If 200 primary spermatocytes and 200 primary oocytes complete gametogenesis, the number of sperms and ova formed will respectively be
questions.solution: Each primary spermatocyte forms 4 sperms (200 x 4 = 800), while each primary oocyte forms only 1 ovum plus polar bodies (200 x 1 = 200).

questions.q_text: The acrosome of a human sperm is formed from
questions.solution: During spermiogenesis the Golgi complex of the spermatid transforms into the cap-like acrosome filled with hydrolytic enzymes.

questions.q_text: Rupture of the Graafian follicle and release of the ovum during the menstrual cycle is induced by
questions.opt_b: A rapid secretion of LH reaching a peak (LH surge)
questions.solution: Both LH and FSH attain a peak in the mid-cycle, but it is the rapid LH surge around day 14 that induces rupture of the Graafian follicle.

questions.q_text: Maintenance of the endometrium in a state necessary for implantation of the blastocyst is mainly due to
questions.solution: The corpus luteum secretes large amounts of progesterone, which is essential for maintenance of the endometrium for implantation.

questions.q_text: Which of the following hormones is NOT produced by the human placenta?
questions.solution: The placenta secretes hCG, hPL, oestrogens, progestogens and later relaxin; FSH is a hormone of the anterior pituitary.

questions.q_text: The stage of the developing embryo that gets implanted in the uterine wall is the
questions.solution: The trophoblast layer of the blastocyst attaches to the endometrium and the blastocyst becomes embedded in it during implantation.

questions.q_text: In the human female, fertilisation of the ovum by the sperm normally takes place at the
questions.solution: Fertilisation occurs only if the ovum and sperms are transported simultaneously to the ampullary-isthmic junction of the oviduct.

questions.q_text: Ejection of milk from the mammary glands during suckling is brought about by
questions.solution: Oxytocin from the posterior pituitary causes contraction of the myoepithelial cells of the mammary alveoli, causing milk ejection.

questions.q_text: The colostrum secreted by the mother during the initial days of lactation is rich in
questions.solution: Colostrum contains several antibodies, predominantly IgA, which is absolutely essential to develop resistance in the newborn.

questions.q_text: At the time of puberty, the number of primary oocytes left in each human ovary is about
questions.solution: About 1 to 2 million primary oocytes are present in each ovary at birth, and only 60,000 to 80,000 remain in each ovary at puberty.

questions.q_text: 'Saheli', the oral contraceptive developed by scientists at CDRI, Lucknow, is
questions.opt_a: A non-steroidal pill taken once a week
questions.solution: Saheli is a non-steroidal 'once a week' oral pill with very few side effects and high contraceptive value.

questions.q_text: Which of the following is a hormone releasing intrauterine device?
questions.solution: LNG-20 and Progestasert are hormone releasing IUDs; Lippes loop is non-medicated and Cu T and Multiload 375 are copper releasing.

questions.q_text: Lactational amenorrhea can be relied upon as a contraceptive method only up to a maximum period of
questions.solution: Ovulation and hence the cycle do not occur during intense lactation, but this method is effective only up to a maximum of six months following parturition.

questions.q_text: Medical termination of pregnancy is considered relatively safe only up to
questions.solution: MTPs are relatively safe during the first trimester, that is up to twelve weeks; second trimester abortions are far more risky.

questions.q_text: In tubectomy, a small part is removed or tied up from the
questions.solution: Tubectomy is female sterilisation in which a small part of the fallopian tube is removed or tied up through a small abdominal or vaginal incision.

questions.q_text: Transfer of an ovum collected from a donor into the fallopian tube of another female who cannot produce an ovum but can provide a suitable environment for fertilisation is called
questions.solution: GIFT, gamete intra fallopian transfer, is the transfer of a donor ovum into the fallopian tube of a recipient female.

questions.q_text: An embryo with more than eight blastomeres is transferred into the uterus in the technique known as
questions.solution: Embryos up to the 8 blastomere stage are transferred into the fallopian tube (ZIFT), while those with more than 8 blastomeres go into the uterus (IUT).

questions.q_text: The specialised procedure in which a sperm is directly injected into the ovum to form an embryo in the laboratory is
questions.solution: Intra cytoplasmic sperm injection involves direct injection of a sperm into the ovum, used mainly in cases of male infertility.

questions.q_text: Emergency contraceptives are effective in avoiding pregnancy if used within
questions.solution: Administration of progestogen-oestrogen combinations or IUDs within 72 hours of coitus is very effective as emergency contraception.

questions.q_text: Which of the following sexually transmitted infections is NOT completely curable?
questions.solution: Except for hepatitis B, genital herpes and HIV infection, other STIs are completely curable if detected early and treated properly.

questions.q_text: Amniocentesis, when used legally, is a foetal diagnostic test that detects
questions.opt_a: The blood group of the mother
questions.opt_b: Only the sex of the foetus
questions.opt_d: Chromosomal abnormalities and genetic disorders of the foetus
questions.solution: Amniocentesis analyses foetal cells in amniotic fluid to detect chromosomal and genetic disorders; its misuse for sex determination is banned.

questions.q_text: Copper releasing intrauterine devices such as Cu T act mainly by
questions.opt_b: Releasing Cu ions that suppress sperm motility and fertilising capacity
questions.opt_c: Making the cervix impassable by surgery
questions.solution: The Cu ions released by copper IUDs suppress sperm motility and the fertilising capacity of sperms in the uterus.

questions.q_text: Which contraceptive method, besides preventing conception, also helps protect the user from sexually transmitted infections?
questions.solution: Condoms cover the genitalia and prevent contact of body fluids, so they also protect the user from STIs and AIDS.

questions.q_text: Malaria is transmitted to humans by the bite of
questions.solution: Only the female Anopheles mosquito acts as the vector of Plasmodium, since it feeds on blood.

questions.q_text: The stage of Plasmodium that enters the human body through the bite of the mosquito is the
questions.solution: Sporozoites stored in the salivary gland of the infected female Anopheles are the infective stage introduced into the human host.

questions.q_text: The chill and high fever recurring every three to four days in malaria is caused by
questions.opt_b: Haemozoin released when infected red blood cells rupture
questions.opt_c: Sporozoites entering the salivary gland of the mosquito
questions.opt_d: Fusion of male and female gametocytes
questions.solution: Haemozoin, a toxic substance released when parasitised RBCs burst, is responsible for the characteristic chill and recurring high fever.

questions.q_text: The common round worm Ascaris lumbricoides is transmitted to humans mainly through
questions.opt_a: Water, vegetables and fruits contaminated with its eggs
questions.opt_b: The bite of an infected mosquito
questions.opt_c: Sexual contact with an infected person
questions.opt_d: Inhalation of droplets from a patient
questions.solution: Eggs of Ascaris passed out with faeces contaminate soil, water, vegetables and fruits, and infect a healthy person on ingestion.

questions.q_text: Elephantiasis, in which the lymphatic vessels of the lower limbs are chronically inflamed, is caused by
questions.solution: Wuchereria bancrofti and W. malayi, the filarial worms, block the lymphatic vessels of the lower limbs causing elephantiasis.

questions.q_text: Which of the following pairs of organisms are both causative agents of ringworm?
questions.solution: Ringworm is caused by the fungal genera Microsporum, Trichophyton and Epidermophyton.

questions.q_text: The Widal test is used for the confirmatory diagnosis of
questions.solution: Typhoid fever caused by Salmonella typhi is confirmed by the Widal test.

questions.q_text: The mechanical carrier that transmits the parasite of amoebiasis from the faeces of an infected person to food is
questions.solution: Houseflies act as mechanical carriers, transmitting cysts of Entamoeba histolytica from infected faeces to food and water.

questions.q_text: Which of the following is a secondary lymphoid organ?
questions.solution: Bone marrow and thymus are primary lymphoid organs; spleen, lymph nodes, tonsils, Peyer's patches and appendix are secondary lymphoid organs.

questions.q_text: An antibody molecule is represented as
questions.solution: Each antibody has four peptide chains, two heavy and two light, hence it is written as H2L2.

questions.q_text: The symptoms of an allergic reaction such as sneezing and watery eyes are due to the release of
questions.opt_c: Histamine and serotonin from mast cells
questions.solution: Allergens trigger IgE-mediated release of chemicals like histamine and serotonin from mast cells, which is why antihistamines give relief.

questions.q_text: Which of the following is an example of passive immunity?
questions.opt_b: Recovery from an attack of chickenpox
questions.opt_d: Tetanus antitoxin injected after an injury
questions.solution: Passive immunity is the direct transfer of ready-made antibodies, as in the preformed antitoxin given for tetanus.

questions.q_text: In HIV, the enzyme that produces viral DNA using the viral RNA as a template is
questions.solution: HIV is a retrovirus whose reverse transcriptase makes a DNA copy of its RNA genome, which is then incorporated into the host DNA.

questions.q_text: Cellular genes that are present in a normal cell and lead to cancer only when activated under certain conditions are called
questions.solution: Cellular oncogenes or c-onc present in normal cells are called proto-oncogenes; on activation they become oncogenes and transform cells.

questions.q_text: In the name of the restriction enzyme EcoRI, the letter 'R' stands for
questions.opt_d: The strain RY13 of the bacterium
questions.solution: In EcoRI, E is for Escherichia, co for coli, R for the strain RY13 and the Roman numeral I for the order of isolation from that strain.

questions.q_text: EcoRI recognises the palindromic sequence GAATTC and cleaves the strand between
questions.solution: EcoRI cuts the DNA a little away from the centre of the palindrome, between G and A on both strands, leaving single stranded sticky ends.

questions.q_text: Which of the following represents a palindromic sequence recognised by restriction endonucleases?
questions.solution: A palindrome in DNA reads the same on both strands when read in the same 5' to 3' direction, as in GAATTC and its complement CTTAAG.

questions.q_text: The enzymes referred to as 'molecular scissors' in recombinant DNA technology are
questions.solution: Restriction endonucleases cut DNA at specific recognition sequences and are therefore called molecular scissors.

questions.q_text: If a foreign DNA fragment is ligated at the BamHI site of the vector pBR322, the recombinant bacteria will lose resistance to
questions.solution: The BamHI site lies within the tetracycline resistance gene, so insertion inactivates it while ampicillin resistance is retained.

questions.q_text: In the blue-white selection method using the enzyme beta-galactosidase, the recombinant colonies appear
questions.solution: Insertion of foreign DNA inactivates the gene for beta-galactosidase, so recombinants cannot produce the blue colour and remain colourless.

questions.q_text: The Ti plasmid widely used as a vector for delivering genes into plant cells is obtained from
questions.solution: The tumour inducing Ti plasmid of Agrobacterium tumefaciens is modified into a disarmed vector for transferring genes into plants.

questions.q_text: Bacterial cells are made competent to take up recombinant DNA by
questions.opt_a: Treating them with a specific divalent cation such as calcium followed by a brief heat shock at 42 degree C
questions.opt_b: Treating them with monovalent sodium ions at 4 degree C
questions.opt_c: Digesting their wall with lysozyme and freezing them
questions.opt_d: Treating them with cellulase and chitinase
questions.solution: Divalent calcium ions increase the efficiency of DNA entry through pores in the cell wall, and a brief heat shock at 42 degree C completes uptake.

questions.q_text: In the polymerase chain reaction, extension of the primers at about 72 degree C is carried out by
questions.solution: Taq polymerase, isolated from Thermus aquaticus, remains active at the high denaturation temperature and extends the primers at about 72 degree C.

questions.q_text: Starting from a single double stranded DNA molecule, the number of copies obtained after four complete cycles of PCR is
questions.solution: Each PCR cycle doubles the DNA, so after n cycles the number of copies is 2 raised to n, that is 2^4 = 16.

questions.q_text: During agarose gel electrophoresis, DNA fragments move towards the
questions.opt_a: Cathode, because DNA is positively charged
questions.opt_b: Cathode, because DNA is negatively charged
questions.opt_c: Anode, because DNA is negatively charged
questions.opt_d: Anode, because DNA is positively charged
questions.solution: The phosphate backbone makes DNA negatively charged, so the fragments migrate towards the positive electrode, the anode.

questions.q_text: Which enzyme is used to break open plant cells for the isolation of genetic material?
questions.solution: Plant cell walls are made of cellulose and are digested by cellulase; lysozyme is used for bacteria and chitinase for fungi.

questions.q_text: Purified DNA finally precipitates out as fine threads when the extract is treated with
questions.solution: Addition of chilled ethanol precipitates DNA, which can be seen as a collection of fine threads in the suspension.

questions.q_text: Inside the bacterium Bacillus thuringiensis, the Bt toxin exists as
questions.opt_a: An inactive protoxin in the form of crystals
questions.opt_b: An active toxin that kills the bacterium
questions.solution: The Bt toxin is produced as inactive protoxin crystals, so the bacterium itself is not killed by the toxin.

questions.q_text: The Bt protoxin ingested by an insect is converted into the active toxin because of
questions.opt_a: The strongly acidic pH of the insect gut
questions.opt_b: The alkaline pH of the insect gut which solubilises the crystals
questions.opt_c: The neutral pH of the insect gut
questions.opt_d: The high body temperature of the insect
questions.solution: The alkaline pH of the insect gut solubilises the crystals, releasing the active toxin that binds midgut epithelial cells and creates pores.

questions.q_text: Which genes code for the proteins that control the cotton bollworms?
questions.solution: The proteins encoded by cryIAc and cryIIAb control the cotton bollworms, while cryIAb controls the corn borer.

questions.q_text: Resistance against the nematode Meloidogyne incognita was developed in tobacco plants by introducing nematode specific genes that produce
questions.opt_c: Both sense and antisense RNA which form a double stranded RNA and silence the nematode mRNA
questions.opt_d: Restriction endonucleases that cut nematode DNA
questions.solution: Using Agrobacterium vectors, sense and antisense RNAs are produced which pair to form dsRNA, initiating RNA interference and silencing the parasite mRNA.

questions.q_text: Mature human insulin consists of
questions.opt_a: Two polypeptide chains, A and B, linked together by disulphide bridges
questions.opt_c: Three polypeptide chains A, B and C
questions.solution: Insulin has a short chain A and a longer chain B held together by disulphide bridges; the C peptide of proinsulin is removed during maturation.

questions.q_text: In mature human insulin, the A chain and the B chain contain how many amino acids respectively?
questions.solution: The A chain of human insulin has 21 amino acids and the B chain has 30 amino acids.

questions.q_text: The first clinical gene therapy, given in 1990 to a four year old girl, was for the treatment of
questions.solution: The first gene therapy was given for adenosine deaminase deficiency, an enzyme defect that causes severe combined immunodeficiency.

questions.q_text: A permanent cure for adenosine deaminase deficiency by gene therapy would be possible if the functional ADA gene is introduced into
questions.opt_a: Bone marrow stem cells at an early embryonic stage
questions.opt_b: Mature lymphocytes infused periodically into the patient
questions.opt_c: Liver cells of the adult patient
questions.solution: Lymphocytes infused into the patient are not immortal, so the treatment must be repeated; introducing the gene into bone marrow stem cells at an early stage would be a permanent cure.

questions.q_text: The ELISA technique used in disease diagnosis is based on the principle of
questions.solution: ELISA, the enzyme linked immunosorbent assay, detects either the antigen or the antibodies against the pathogen through antigen-antibody interaction.

questions.q_text: Rosie, the first transgenic cow, produced milk that was enriched with
questions.solution: Rosie produced human protein enriched milk containing 2.4 grams per litre of human alpha-lactalbumin, making it more balanced for human babies.

questions.q_text: GEAC, the body set up by the Indian Government to examine the safety of introducing GM organisms, stands for
questions.solution: The Genetic Engineering Approval Committee takes decisions on the validity of GM research and the safety of introducing GM organisms for public services.

questions.q_text: The use of bio-resources by multinational companies and organisations without proper authorisation from the countries concerned is called
questions.solution: Biopiracy is the exploitation of bio-resources and traditional knowledge without authorisation or compensatory payment, as in the Basmati and neem cases.

questions.q_text: In the commercial production of human insulin using recombinant DNA technology by Eli Lilly, the mature hormone was obtained by
questions.opt_a: Expressing the entire proinsulin gene with its C peptide in yeast
questions.opt_b: Extracting insulin from cultured human pancreatic cells
questions.opt_c: Removing the C peptide enzymatically inside the bacterial cell
questions.opt_d: Preparing the A and B chains separately in Escherichia coli and combining them by creating disulphide bonds
questions.solution: Two DNA sequences corresponding to chains A and B were introduced into E. coli separately and the chains produced were then combined by creating disulphide bonds.

questions.q_text: The experiment in which methane, hydrogen, ammonia and water vapour were circulated at 800 degree C in a closed flask with electric discharge was performed by
questions.opt_a: S. L. Miller and H. Urey
questions.solution: Miller and Urey created conditions similar to the primitive atmosphere and obtained amino acids, supporting chemical evolution.

questions.q_text: The idea that the first form of life arose slowly from pre-existing non-living organic molecules was proposed by
questions.solution: Oparin of Russia and Haldane of England proposed chemical evolution, that life arose from pre-existing non-living organic molecules such as RNA and proteins.

questions.q_text: The forelimbs of whales, bats, cheetahs and humans having a similar anatomical structure is an example of
questions.solution: Similar structures performing different functions and inherited from a common ancestor are homologous and represent divergent evolution.

questions.q_text: Which of the following pairs represents analogous structures?
questions.opt_a: Thorn of Bougainvillea and tendril of Cucurbita
questions.opt_b: Forelimb of a bat and flipper of a whale
questions.opt_c: Wings of a butterfly and wings of a bird
questions.solution: Butterfly and bird wings differ anatomically but perform the same function of flight, so they are analogous and show convergent evolution.

questions.q_text: Industrial melanism observed in the peppered moth Biston betularia in England is a classic example of
questions.solution: After industrialisation the tree trunks darkened, so dark winged moths survived better than white winged ones, showing selection by predators.

questions.q_text: The variety of beaks seen among Darwin's finches on the Galapagos Islands is best explained as
questions.solution: From one original seed eating stock many forms with altered beaks evolved in the same geographical area to suit different food habits, that is adaptive radiation.

questions.q_text: Which of the following does NOT disturb the Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium of a population?
questions.opt_b: Random mating in a very large population
questions.solution: The equilibrium p^2 + 2pq + q^2 = 1 holds when mating is random in a large population with no migration, mutation, drift or selection.

questions.q_text: In a population in Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium, 4 per cent of the individuals show a recessive disorder. The percentage of carriers in the population is
questions.solution: q^2 = 0.04 so q = 0.2 and p = 0.8; carriers are 2pq = 2 x 0.8 x 0.2 = 0.32, that is 32 per cent.

questions.q_text: In a population at Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium, 9 per cent of individuals are homozygous recessive. The percentage of homozygous dominant individuals is
questions.solution: q^2 = 0.09 so q = 0.3 and p = 0.7; homozygous dominants are p^2 = 0.49, that is 49 per cent.

questions.q_text: The brain capacity of Homo habilis, the first human-like being, was about
questions.solution: Homo habilis had a brain capacity between 650 and 800 cc and probably did not eat meat.

questions.q_text: Neanderthal man, with a brain size of about 1400 cc, lived in the Near East and central Asia between
questions.solution: Neanderthals lived between about 1,00,000 and 40,000 years back and used hides to protect their bodies and buried their dead.

questions.q_text: Fossils of Homo erectus, discovered in Java in 1891 and dated to about 1.5 million years ago, indicate a brain capacity of about
questions.solution: Homo erectus had a large brain of around 900 cc and probably ate meat.

questions.q_text: Lamarck's theory of evolution is based on
questions.opt_a: Use and disuse of organs and inheritance of acquired characters
questions.opt_d: Random genetic drift in small populations
questions.solution: Lamarck proposed that organs used more develop further and such acquired characters are passed on to the next generation.
